_comment: mini-dudeai FEDERATOR seed — the primary/manager box (the one that runs the :5000 federator + situation digest). Runs watchdog + federation + digest sources (MINI_DUDEAI_ENABLE_FEDERATION/_ENABLE_DIGEST default on); gateway boxes use mini_dudeai_rules.fleet_gateway.json instead (watchdog-only). Per-box file at ~/mini_dudeai_rules.json; the daemon promotes ~/mini_dudeai_rules.json.candidate over it on the next tick. Repo canonical for backup + re-deploy parity with the gateway seed (closes the federator repo-parity gap, 2026-05-31).

rules.annotation: Issue #69 — foreign daemon hijacked @rns/<instance>. Recovery: stop the foreign daemon, restart rnsd, restart RNS-using services.
Issue #68 — main thread silent-stuck in syscall while background threads keep logging. Check /proc/PID/task/PID/stack.
Issue #61 / #70 / #71 class — GIL-bound serialization or socketserver deadlock. Check cache hit-rates at /api/status.{directory,geojson,topology}.cache.
Issue #63 — write-path silent failure (sandbox path drift). Audit ReadWritePaths= against actual write sites.
Listener UP + no SYN-SENT pile-up but new connects hang. Recovery: systemctl restart rnsd.service then restart RNS-using services.

moc3 is gateway-only; permanent federation backoff is EXPECTED. Annotates digest only — no ntfy. Catch-all unexpected-peer rule deferred to post-soak (needs subject_exclude_globs support to not re-fire moc3).

B2 (2026-05-28): unexpected unhealthy federation peer; subject_exclude_globs skips moc3 (handled by moc3_federation_backoff_known_normal). Side-effect-free escalation -> history for the cloud session to chase; NO ntfy page. Per-box pattern (2026-05-31): operator boxes may add a local *_federation_known_normal rule (annotate_digest) plus a matching subject_exclude_globs entry for a KNOWN cross-project peer that surfaces as a bare IP (peer_name=null) — e.g. the MeshAnchor host meshanchor-server. Such rules live in that box's own ~/mini_dudeai_rules.json because the addresses are operator-specific (MF014); they are deliberately NOT in this repo seed.
meshforge-digest.service may be down or wedged. systemctl --user status meshforge-digest
watchdog.json unreadable — meshforge-watchdog.service may be down.

/api/status unreachable — meshforge-map.service may be down (see Issue #68 detection recipe). grace_s=90 debounces our own meshforge-map restart blips (~30s, self-clearing); a real >90s federator outage still pages.

Issue #69 — foreign daemon owns @rns/<instance> (often lab.lxmf_tracer winning the @rns race during an rnsd cycle); the box's RNS is broken until reclaimed. Recovery: stop the foreign daemon, `sudo systemctl restart rnsd.service`, restart RNS-using services. Verify owner is rnsd: `sudo ss -xnpl | grep @rns/`. Companion to the ntfy page rns_namespace_collision_any — surfaces it in the deep-feed/brief 'look here first'.

2026-06-01: born-correct permission foundation drifted (mf.4/#73) — /etc/reticulum perms wrong for the non-root rnsd; latent (works until the next logfile rotation, then RNS.log() fails every write). Fix: sudo scripts/fleet_foundation.py apply (no restart). Side-effect-free escalation -> brief/deep-rollup; NO ntfy page (degraded, not an active outage).

2026-06-01: MeshForge<->MeshAnchor RNS-reliability parity drift (lead-repo port debt). Only fires where /opt/meshanchor is present (the box holding both repos). Fix: port the flagged change, verify python3 scripts/parity_check.py. Side-effect-free escalation; NO ntfy page.

2026-06-01: installed rns/lxmf off the +mf.N fork pin (box missed a fork roll). Fix: reviewed pip install --force-reinstall -r requirements/rns.txt, then verify rnsd. Side-effect-free escalation; NO ntfy page.

2026-07-19: rns/lxmf copies across this box's envs DISAGREE (a roll/install missed a pipx venv or user-site copy -- the moc3 nomadnet-venv lesson; one shared rnsd => every env must carry the identical RNS substrate). Fix: reinstall the odd env(s) to the box's consumer version (pipx runpip <venv> install --force-reinstall -r requirements/rns.txt), re-verify. Side-effect-free escalation; NO ntfy page.

2026-07-19: an enrolled always-on USER .service is not running (parked failed / stopped-and-forgotten / user manager down with linger off -- the #79 class; nomadnet_crashloop covers only a LIVE loop). Check: systemctl --user status <unit>; recover: systemctl --user reset-failed <unit> && systemctl --user start <unit>; manager-down: loginctl enable-linger <operator>. Side-effect-free escalation; NO ntfy page.

2026-06-12: a critical pip dep (meshtastic) installed BELOW the requirements/core.txt floor in the service user's env — a box that missed/failed an update (the recurring update/install/env class, feedback_version_env_rigor). Fix: pip3 install --break-system-packages --upgrade <pkg> (or the TUI Update), then verify version + import in the service user python. Side-effect-free escalation; NO ntfy page (degraded).

2026-06-17: meshtastic installed at DIVERGENT versions across root-readable locations (venv / system-wide dist-packages / root+user pipx / user-site) with ≥1 copy BELOW the core.txt floor — the service consumer-of-record can be fine while the TUI-as-root reads a stale stray and shows phantom 'update available' (the install-fragmentation half of the update class, feedback_version_env_rigor; dep_version_drift sees only the consumer). Fix: reconcile every copy to >= the floor via python3 scripts/meshtastic_install_audit.py (see its --fix hint), then re-check. Side-effect-free escalation; NO ntfy page (degraded).

2026-06-03: live systemd unit state diverges from the box's declared role (fleet_roles.yaml + deployment.json overrides) — the moc2 legibility class. Documented service_overrides do NOT fire. Fix: review python3 scripts/provision_role.py, then sudo --apply or correct the declared role. Side-effect-free escalation; NO ntfy page (degraded, not an outage).

2026-06-21 upstream-app ownership Action 5: an INHERITED (non-Nursedude-origin) upstream app checkout carries an unversioned tracked-file CODE patch — a hand-edit that exists in no repo we control and is one `git pull` from silent deletion (the rescued .32 + dev-box bot patches were exactly this; policy §4.2). Fix: rescue the patch into an owned fork or the tracked overlay (Nursedude/fleet-overlays), or upstream it as a PR, then converge the checkout clean and record the pin in fleet-overlays/PINS.md. Side-effect-free escalation; NO ntfy page (degraded, latent version-control hygiene debt, not an outage).

Issue #72 — rnsd accepts the shared-instance socket but the RPC round-trip hangs (rnstatus times out though the listener accepts). Recovery: sudo systemctl restart rnsd, then restart RNS-using services (meshforge-map, tracer).
#68 family — a TCPInterface is Down while its peer is TCP-reachable (stuck uplink that won't self-heal). Check rnstatus interface state; bounce rnsd or the uplink interface.

Issue #73 — open fds approaching the soft RLIMIT_NOFILE (proactive companion to http_local; fires BEFORE :5000 wedges with [Errno 24]). Restart the service to clear, then find the fd leak (sudo ls /proc/PID/fd | wc -l).

2026-06-04 .32 dark-feed lesson: hours of zero decoded text on the meshforge channel while the json-uplink pipeline is alive = missed PSK re-key (decode gate = hash(name,psk)), deaf radio (channel_utilization=0.0 tell), or dead uplink. Send a ch2 test from another fleet box to discriminate.

MF Issue #74 (2026-06-06): persistent-queue depth near the shed threshold (>=80%/95% of max -> LOW/NORMAL loss) or dead-letter growth per tick. Backlog masks delivery failures. Check /api/gateway/queue + gateway journal for the failing destination.

MF Issue #74 (2026-06-06): sends keep flowing but the recent-ring confirm rate collapsed (<=50% degraded, <=10% wedge, >=20 ring sends). The bridge self-report reads HEALTHY while shouting into a void — check RNS paths to fan-out peers + /api/gateway/delivery drop_reasons.

MF synth-soak watch (2026-06-15): the hourly LXMF round-trip exerciser (meshforge-synth-soak.timer) FAILED its delivery envelope (pass_envelope=false) or went DARK (no fresh result in ~2.5 cadences). The synth canary was previously unwatched — the fire script always exits 0 and nothing consumed pass_envelope. Check meshforge-synth-soak.timer (systemd --user) + ~/.local/state/meshforge/synth_soak/fire.log; for an envelope fail, the detail carries the worst pair — also check /api/gateway/delivery drop_reasons. Self-guards INERT on boxes that don't run the soak.

Box hard-reset with no clean shutdown (BootHealthSource; wired 2026-06-06 after the primary box's 3rd power-cut). Forensic method: tail ~/power_history.log (throttled bit 0x10000 = brownout occurred; 0x0 throughout = instant external cut) + journalctl -b -1 -o short-precise | tail (healthy-then-cut = hard reset; grep oom-kill/panic). Full method in the hard-reset memory topic file.
Crash forensic seed for the next warm cloud session — surfaces the unclean-boot verdict + last pre-cut power reading in situation_digest.

Issue #75 — an unaccounted persistent TCP to meshtasticd :4403 is draining the PhoneAPI stream (web client goes deaf to inbound texts/ACKs while the radio journal shows healthy RX). Recovery: sudo systemctl restart meshforge-map.service, then verify /api/radio/status persistent_owner.

2026-06-13→15 moc incident — ≥2 contending single-consumers thrash meshtasticd's :4403 ('Force close previous TCP connection' churn, #17/#75 class), wedging the gateway's stateless-HTTP-protobuf mesh-TX: bot output stops reaching nodes while the RNS round-trip canary stays green (mesh-RF leg unwatched). Recovery: sudo systemctl restart meshtasticd, then stop the 2nd consumer (typically the map's _collect_meshtasticd :4403 source).

Issue #77 — the radio's OBSERVED publish root diverged from the box's DECLARED consumer root (zero-config join or factory reset reintroduces msh/US). This is the CAUSE of the dark-feed class, visible hours before channel_feed_dark proves the symptom. Fix: meshtastic --host localhost --set mqtt.root <declared> (or correct gateway.json if the radio is the intended truth).

Issue #78 — a crontab-wired cron_verdict.sh cron went silent past its cadence, or its latest verdict is FAIL/CONCERN. The silent-cron class: the cron may have been firing into a deleted path for weeks. Check ~/cron_verdicts.log + crontab -l on the box. Side-effect-free escalation; NO ntfy page (degraded, not an outage).

Leg D (2026-06-17) - a fleet box the offline-monitor (fleet_offline_check.sh on the manager box) confirmed UNREACHABLE past its 3-fail (~15min) threshold. Surfaced into the warm brief + /fleet so a dark box can't sit silent in a side-channel logfile (the .32 33h-dark lesson). The monitor OWNS the ntfy re-page (witnessed, escalating); this rule is visibility only - propose_escalation, NO duplicate page.

Leg C (2026-06-17) - the dude-claw out-of-band witness (host_probe over NATS, on the watched box's own subnet) reports a target HOST_FROZEN (kernel alive, userspace swap-wedged - the .32 class the box's self-petted HW watchdog can't catch), UNREACHABLE (host/path/SoC down), or a sustained UNKNOWN (the claw witness itself unreachable = lost visibility, not 'healthy'). Surfaced into the warm brief + /fleet. Alert-only - propose_escalation, NO ntfy; the operator decides on the page.

2026-07-11 OpenWrt-router arc - a mirrored meshforge-scout tick shows the ROUTER-side agent degraded: fresh mirror but stale captured_at (the agent cron died on the router while the pull keeps copying a corpse), tick ok=false (agent's own witnesses: tmpfs data_dir / unreadable proc / dead radio TCP), or an unparseable mirror. Fix: ssh to the router, check its scout crontab + /etc/meshforge/scout.conf, run meshforge-scout check by hand (templates/openwrt/README.md). The pull channel is healthy or this would be cron_verdict_stale instead. degraded only - every observed condition is remote.

ntfy receipt-heartbeat Phase 2 (2026-06-18) - the alerting channel's OWN loopback failed: a manager-box collector (fleet_ntfy_loopback.sh) publishes a nonce'd min-priority heartbeat to the fleet topic and polls ntfy.sh to confirm it loops back; a miss means ntfy.sh is down OR the fleet topic's publish path is broken OR the sender no-ops. The collector OWNS the page and escalates via the Phase-1 EMAIL backbone (ntfy is the suspect channel, so it does NOT page back through ntfy); this rule is visibility only - propose_escalation, NO duplicate page. The operator-phone-on-wrong-topic case is Phase 3's tap-to-ack job.

ntfy receipt-heartbeat Phase 3 (2026-06-18) - the ONLY rung that confirms the operator's DEVICE. A manager-box cron (fleet_ntfy_ack.sh) sends a WEEKLY tap-to-ack page; consecutive unacked weeks mean the phone may not be receiving fleet pages (wrong/dead topic, app killed, notifications off - the exact 06-14->17 failure loopback can't catch, since loopback is a different subscriber). The cron OWNS the page and escalates via the Phase-1 EMAIL backbone at >=2 unacked weeks; this rule is visibility only - propose_escalation, NO duplicate page.

Issue #79 — mini's loop is alive and firing but history.jsonl stopped accumulating (swallowed write failure: perms/owner/disk). The warm-context feed is the casualty. Check file perms + free disk on the mini host. Side-effect-free escalation; NO ntfy page.

Issue #79 — the box's live ~/mini_dudeai_rules.json is missing rule ids its role seed carries (a seed bump didn't reach this box). Fix: merge the new seed rules into the live file via the candidate flow (preserve box-local rules). Side-effect-free escalation; NO ntfy page.

Issue #79 — MEMORY.md crept over the ~24KB context-load limit; sessions silently partial-load the index. Remedy: demote older/shipped entries to MEMORY_ARCHIVE.md (mini_dudeai.memory_apply.demote_memory). Side-effect-free escalation; NO ntfy page.

2026-06-09 version-updates arc — a newer same-flavor kernel is installed under /lib/modules than the running one (or /var/run/reboot-required exists); moc1 ran 6.12.75 for days with 6.18.33 installed and nothing paged. Fix: schedule a clean reboot (planned reboots through clean shutdown record boot_health clean-exit). Side-effect-free escalation; NO ntfy page (degraded, not an outage).

2026-07-10 (upstream meshtastic/firmware#10468, operator's own 2026-05-13 report): meshtasticd on Pi5+USB leaks exited pthread stacks; VSZ past the weekly-restart envelope (768 GB) means meshtasticd-restart.timer missed or the leak rate worsened. Fix: systemctl restart meshtasticd, then verify the timer (systemctl list-timers meshtasticd-restart.timer). Side-effect-free escalation; degraded, not an outage.

AREDN Phase 0 (2026-06-12) — a box with aredn_node_ips configured whose local AREDN sysinfo collection went dark: node unreachable, or the running service predates the config (reports not_configured while the settings file carries IPs — restart meshforge-map to load). The worldmap fallback masks the loss; found dormant on the AREDN-site box itself. Side-effect-free escalation; NO ntfy page (degraded — the map serves, the AREDN leg is blind).

Calibration spine (2026-06-15) -- a VERIFIED completion claim (Claude's 'done/100%/all green') did NOT hold when re-derived against external ground truth (a full honest_status verdict on the head it was claimed on later FAILED). Surfaces 'you said 100% and the math was wrong' as a tracked number instead of a private impression. SSOT .claude/rules/calibrated_claims.md. Side-effect-free escalation; NO ntfy page until the re-derivation soaks low-false-positive (degraded, a trust signal not an outage).

2026-06-19 — the NomadNet user unit is crashlooping (the NRestarts=7842, 10-day-silent class; probe_service_inactive is structurally blind to user units). Usually exit 75 from the rnstatus boot-gate (rnsd not hosting) or exit 87 rpc_key mismatch. Check: journalctl --user -u nomadnet -n 50; systemctl --user status nomadnet. Recovery: fix the start-pre gate / rpc_key, then systemctl --user restart nomadnet.

2026-06-19 — companion to nomadnet_crashloop_any; surfaces the crashloop in the deep-feed/brief 'look here first' so a session catches an episode the posture pane no longer shows. Cross-refs the #69-fix-regression (the rnstatus boot-gate).

2026-06-20 gateway-reliability arc A2 -- the gateway's OWN journal self-report shows it is NOT delivering: leg 1 = windowed delivered/attempted ratio collapse (recent, high-volume; conservative floor because the journal's total-dropped folds in benign Mesh->RNS broadcast misses -- the precise lens is delivery_confirmation_stall), leg 2 = a spike of EROFS / resource-assembly / forward-to-secondary errors (the exact 2026-06-20 wx-total-loss witness that had a journal witness but no probe consumer; an EROFS spike is the #60 sandbox class -- confirm meshforge-gateway.service ReadWritePaths includes /etc/reticulum/storage). OUTCOME monitor: the gateway may read 'active / RNS: connected' while replies silently drop. Self-guards INERT off a box that doesn't run meshforge-gateway.

2026-06-20 gateway-reliability arc A1 (the OUTCOME source of truth) -- the synthetic RESOURCE round-trip canary (meshforge-gateway-resource-canary.timer -> src/lab/gateway_resource_canary) FAILED its verdict or went DARK. A1 actively PROVES the gateway delivers a multi-chunk RNS Resource round-trip -- the exact path the 2026-06-20 wx-total-loss EROFS broke while single-packet replies kept working (so every shape/liveness probe and the single-packet gateway_rt_canary read green). The canary fires a control PING + a PINGBIG whose reply is resource-sized; its own FAIL 'control back, resource NOT' is the EROFS signature (check the gateway journal for EROFS / 'assembling received resource' + that meshforge-gateway.service ReadWritePaths includes /etc/reticulum/storage). A stale envelope = the canary went silent. Self-guards INERT off a box that doesn't run the canary; the 'canary itself must be watched' pattern, mirroring synth_soak_degraded.

2026-06-22 mesh-oracle health -- the read-only 'ask dude-AI over the mesh' responder (src/oracle) answered queries but its confirmable delivery rate (delivered / (delivered + send_errors), over a recent ts window of ~/.local/share/meshforge/mesh_oracle_log.jsonl) fell below threshold. Intentional declines (cooldown / not_allowlisted) and benign non-deliveries (reason-less delivered:false -- RNS no-path to an unannounced ephemeral identity / MeshCore restart race) are EXCLUDED from the failure set + surfaced in the signal extra, so this is the #74 confirmation view, not a false alarm on a cooldowned/quiet channel. WITNESSED v1 blind spot: the RNS leg's send_to_rns swallows real send exceptions to a bare False, so an RNS send error lands in the benign bucket (the Meshtastic/MQTT/MeshCore legs surface send_error fully) -- the benign count makes the RNS gap visible. Check the gateway's RNS/Meshtastic send path + the oracle audit log on the box. Side-effect-free escalation; NO ntfy page (degraded, not an outage -- low-traffic read-only service). Self-guards INERT off a box where the oracle never wrote a log (disabled / never queried).

2026-06-30 dedup/identity arc STEP 6 -- HUMAN-facing cross-gateway DUPLICATE delivery from the 4c /fleet/dups rollup: the same (content_id, recipient) CONFIRMED on >1 DISTINCT gateway. The JOIN now classifies the recipient INFRA (itself a gateway/peer hash -- e.g. MeshAnchor 58cecbd0, in BOTH gateways' peer_gateway_destinations, so both legitimately relay there) vs HUMAN (a real NomadNet inbox). This rung pages ONLY on HUMAN dups -- the real reliability defect; the infra-to-infra dup is real but benign AND structurally unsuppressable with zero added loss + no coordination substrate (two gateways confirm-deliver the same content simultaneously; copy #2 can't be cancelled after the fact), so it is surfaced in the detail but NOT paged. degraded only -- a dup is a quality/cost defect, not an outage (delivery still happened). The probe (probe_gateway_dup_degraded) reads /fleet/dups on the manager box; INERT when the rollup is indeterminate (<2 gateways) or stale (dead collector cron); 2-tick debounce. Investigate /fleet/dups fleet_duplicates[] where recipient_kind==human. STEP-0 reconciliation: the earlier 'replace the is_already_bridged loop guard with an identity-based one' C-fix framing was DROPPED -- the bot is mesh node !a2e95ba4 emitting RAW text so the loop guard never drops its reply; the real problem-C fix is identity-correlation (a separate future slice).
